text: A calamity is a terrible event that causes huge damage or suffering. Japan's minister wants the country ready for the worst ones.
Vigilance means watching carefully for danger, even when things seem fine. With stranger weather, people must stay alert for new kinds of threats.
To streamline is to make something simpler and smoother by cutting extra steps. The agency should make disaster planning less tangled.
Tectonic plates are giant slabs of rock that make up Earth's outer layer. They move very slowly, and earthquakes happen where their edges push and slip.
A bureaucracy is the many offices and workers of a government, each with its own job. Here, those offices had trouble working together.
Bureaucracies are government offices and agencies. Japan keeps creating new ones for new problems.
Prone to something means likely to suffer it. A country prone to disasters gets hit often.
To spawn is to produce or create something, often a lot of it. Japan keeps spawning new government agencies.
An agency is an organization in the government set up to handle one kind of job. This one handles disasters.
To bat away an idea means to push it aside without really thinking about it, like swatting a fly. Governments kept rejecting a disaster agency.
A minister is a high government official in charge of one area, like disasters. Hosono Goshi is the new one.
Freshly means just now or very recently. A freshly appointed minister has only just got the job.
Appointed means chosen for a job by someone in charge, instead of being voted in.
To vow is to make a very serious promise. The minister promised to make Japan the most prepared nation.
On the scale of means as big as. A disaster on the scale of a national crisis would hurt the whole country.
A junction is a place where things meet, like roads crossing. Four plates meet under Japan.
Magnitude is a number that tells how strong an earthquake is. A magnitude 7 quake is very powerful.
A tsunami is a giant sea wave, usually caused by an earthquake under the ocean floor.
A nuclear meltdown is a serious accident at a nuclear power plant, when the reactor overheats and is damaged. It followed the 2011 tsunami.
A peninsula is land with water on three sides, like a finger sticking out into the sea.
Devastated means badly damaged or destroyed. The Noto peninsula was wrecked by an earthquake in 2024.
Torrential rain is rain that pours down very hard and fast, like a river from the sky.
Intensified means made stronger. Climate change has made heavy rain stronger.
To pose a threat means to be a threat. Floods pose a growing danger.
To be dwarfed means to be made to look small next to something much bigger. Past disasters may look small next to future ones.
Seismologists are scientists who study earthquakes.
Catastrophic means causing huge damage and suffering, like a disaster.
A statistical model uses numbers from the past to guess how likely something is in the future, like a weather forecast.
Probability is how likely something is to happen. A 70% probability means it is quite likely.
A megaquake is an extremely powerful earthquake.
The Nankai Trough is a deep valley in the sea floor off Japan's Pacific coast, where two plates meet. Scientists fear a huge quake there.
To evacuate is to leave a dangerous place to get to safety. 12.3m is 12.3 million people.
GDP is the total value of everything a country makes and sells in a year. It measures how big its economy is.
A blackout is when the electricity goes off over a large area.
A supply chain is the path food and goods take from where they are made to the shops. If it breaks, shelves go empty.
Hardware means physical things, like strong buildings. The article contrasts it with software, which means plans and ways of working.
Here, software does not mean computer programs. It means plans, rules and training, as opposed to physical things.
Seconded means lent for a while to work somewhere else. Officials were lent by other ministries.
To rotate out means to leave a job after your turn so someone else can take over.
A Band-Aid fix covers up a problem without solving its cause, like a bandage on a deep wound.
Institutional knowledge is what an organization has learned over the years. It is lost if experts keep leaving.
Siloed means kept apart, like grain in separate towers. Offices that do not share information are siloed.
Notoriously means in a way that is widely known, usually for something bad.
To co-ordinate is to get different people or groups to work together smoothly.
Sweltering means extremely hot and sticky.
Demography is the makeup of a country's people, such as how many are old or young. Japan has many older people.
Sanitation means clean toilets, clean water and ways to stay germ-free. Without it, people get sick.
Nutritious food is healthy food that gives your body what it needs.
Perseverance means keeping going through hard times without giving up.
To idealise something is to treat it as perfect. Here, people praise survivors who just put up with hardship, even when that hurts them.
To endure is to suffer through something hard without giving up.
Municipalities are towns and cities with their own local governments.
To clamber is to climb using hands and feet, in a clumsy way.
Kawara are traditional Japanese roof tiles. They are heavy, so they can fall in a quake and hurt people.
Rubble is the broken pieces of bricks, wood and concrete left after a building falls.
Lorry is the British word for a truck.
Makeshift means built quickly from whatever is around, for temporary use.
To stockpile is to save up a big supply of something, like food and water, for emergencies.
Kojo is the Japanese word for help from the government.
Kyojo means mutual help, neighbors helping each other.
Jijo means self-help, preparing and protecting yourself. Hosono says it stays essential.
Saigai kanrenshi is Japanese for disaster-related deaths, when survivors later die from stress or poor health.
Bosai is the Japanese word for disaster prevention.
